questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question:
In [Determinants], consider the system of linear equations:
$x + y + z = 6,\; x + 2y + 3z = 10,\; x + 2y + \lambda z = \mu$.
For what values of parameters $\lambda$ and $\mu$ does this system have infinitely many solutions?
questions.solution: Coefficient determinant is $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & \lambda \end{vmatrix} = \lambda - 3$. For infinite solutions, $\Delta = 0 \implies \lambda = 3$. With $\lambda = 3$, the third equation becomes identical to the second only if $\mu = 10$.
questions.explanation: Solve using rigorous mathematical proofs and transformations in Determinants.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question:
Evaluate the integer value of the limit in [Determinants]:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} \times 6$$
questions.solution: Using Taylor series $\sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{6} + O(x^5)$, we have $\frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} = \frac{1}{6} + O(x^2) \to \frac{1}{6}$. Multiplied by $6$, the value is $1$.
questions.explanation: Derive using rigorous mathematical theorems in Determinants.
